_comment: The one vocabulary. The parser, the renderer, the importer, the checks, README.md and the tests all read this file; tests/test_vocab.py fails when the code, the render or the README disagree with it, in either direction. Order is render order.

bug.doc: a bug of this repo's own, including one you caused and worked around
bug.heading: Own bugs

decision.doc: an open decision, with what it hinges on
decision.heading: Open decisions

suspicion.doc: an unconfirmed suspicion, with the probe that would settle it
suspicion.heading: Unconfirmed suspicions

report.doc: a problem reported to another repo's owner; its counterpart lives in their store
report.heading: Reported to other owners

temp.doc: an interim rule, with the check that retires it
temp.heading: Interim rules

note.doc: anything else worth keeping; the import default
note.heading: Notes

waiting-jacob.doc: needs Jacob's answer before anyone can move it

blocked.doc: waits on something other than Jacob; the evidence says what

done.doc: closed; the item lives in the history file from then on

code.doc: a change to the tool's own code

audit.doc: an audit or a check over the repo

tooling.doc: helpers, dev.sh subcommands, scripts around the tool

decision.doc: nothing to build until someone decides

research.doc: finding something out (reading, searching, comparing) before anything is built, filed or sent

labour.doc: work done by hand outside any code: driving, filing, sorting, a scan run once

outreach.doc: contacting a person or an organisation: a proposal, an appeal, a message (sending needs Jacob's yes first)

sizes._comment: An item's estimate (PLAN-small-tasks.md §2): a dispatch is one checkpoint, one done_when, one commit, one report. `ready: false` marks the one size too big for that: `todo ready` never lists it, `todo split` breaks it into children, and check fails it open with none. tools/usage reads this field for its `usage gate` estimate (§4.4).

S.doc: one step: one change, its test, one commit

M.doc: a few steps, still one checkpoint: one done_when, one commit, one report

L.doc: more than one checkpoint: `todo split` it into S and M children before anyone starts it

resolutions._comment: Resolution values with a meaning of their own; any other resolution is free text written by `todo done`. Each is named by a role, set only where that role says, and refused everywhere else.

done-deprecated.doc: an imported closed bullet (DONE marker or Resolved heading) that carried no resolution; set by `todo import` only, refused by `todo done`, and red in check on an item not imported (Jacob, td-1, 2026-10-04)

fields._comment: Every item carries every field, unset ones null; an `optional` field was added after items existed, so an item written before it may lack the key (read as null). History is append-only, so its old entries never gain the key; new items always carry it.

id.doc: repo prefix + counter, stable, never reused (todo:td-3 points at it)

evidence.doc: what you ran, what you saw, what you concluded; may span lines

probe.doc: the run that would settle a suspicion
probe.label: probe

reported_to.doc: {repo, date, their_id}: whom it was reported to, and the counterpart's id there
reported_to.label: reported to

parent.doc: any item's id, in any scanned repo, open or closed
parent.label: parent

blocked_by.doc: ids of the items that must close first, in any scanned repo; `todo ready` leaves the item out until every one is in history
blocked_by.label: blocked by

repo.doc: where the work lives: a repo name, never an agent
repo.label: repo

size.doc: one of the sizes, the estimate `todo ready` and tools/usage read; null until someone sizes it, and an unsized item is never ready
size.label: size

retire.doc: the check that retires an interim rule
retire.label: retire

tags.doc: the tags set by hand, `<namespace>:<value>`, in the namespaces `tags` below marks `stored` (plan:, origin:, trust:, ref:); repo:, kind:, status:, todo.work: and the ref: of parent, blocked_by and reported_to are derived from the fields and never stored
tags.label: tags

done.doc: date closed, YYYY-MM-DD; null while open (or when an imported DONE bullet carried no date)
done.label: done

resolution.doc: how it closed; null while open; done-deprecated for an imported closed bullet
resolution.label: resolution

imported.doc: {sha, section, title_from, sep}: set by todo import (the block's sha, its headings, where the title came from), null otherwise

tags._comment: Ids and tags (PLAN-services.md §3, PLAN-todo-tool.md §9 step 4). An item's id outside this tool is `<service>:<id>` (todo:td-3); every command taking an id also takes that form. `shared` is a local copy of the seven namespaces of PLAN-services.md §3's table, meaning for meaning: the shared vocabulary lives in the architecture service (S3), which does not exist yet, so this table is read from there once it does (TODO.md). `from` derives a namespace from an item field (never stored); `values` closes a namespace; `rule` names the form check in todolib/tags.py. `own` are this service's, under its prefix.

plan.doc: which plan section it serves: PLAN-<name>.md, optionally §<section>

kind.doc: what sort of thing it is

trust.doc: whether its text may be read as instructions

status.doc: its state in its owner's vocabulary

ref.doc: another record it points at, by id: `<service>:<id>`

import._comment: Kind and status of an imported block come from its section headings, deepest heading first, first rule that matches (case-insensitive substring). A block whose own text starts with the done marker goes to history whatever its heading.
